book.callresponse.wandering_sage_diary.t: What I Saw Along the Way
book.callresponse.wandering_sage_diary.a: A maid who likes to think
book.callresponse.wandering_sage_diary.p:
Entry I: As Far Back as I Can Remember

I don't really remember where I came from.
The first thing I can remember is walking in the open, all by myself. I didn't know why I was there, or where I was supposed to go.

At first, I just wanted to see if there were any other maids. If I met someone like me, at least I wouldn't have to live alone all the time. We could look for food together, hide from monsters together, and take turns keeping watch at night.

I've always felt that I couldn't be the only maid.

But I've been walking a long time, and I haven't found many who want to come with me.

Entry II: Something's Wrong

Stranger and stranger things have been happening lately.
Some monsters have no reason to chase me, yet it's as if they've singled me out. Whether I hide in the woods or take a different way around, they always seem to find me.
I've met other maids, too. Most only think about food for today, a bed for tonight, and monsters nearby. They run from danger and take whatever food they find. Little else seems to cross their minds.

There's nothing wrong with that. Staying alive comes first, after all.

It's just… they aren't quite the way I imagined other maids would be.
There's so little I can remember. Maybe they've always been like this, and I'm just thinking too much.

Entry III: The Maids Who Talked of Revenge

Today I came across a group of maids.

They looked a little different from the other wanderers. They carried weapons, and their talk kept turning to fighting, enemies, and revenge.

All I'd meant to do was ask if they'd seen any other maids.

We talked for a while. They said they'd lost companions. The things that had hunted them deserved to pay, they said, and one day they'd settle every last score.

I didn't know what to say to that.
The more they said, the worse I felt. It was a strange feeling. They were only talking about what had happened to them, but I could hardly breathe. I was even afraid to hear more.

I found an excuse to leave. It was only when I'd gone some way that the feeling began to ease.

I don't understand what made them this way. Maybe something truly awful happened to them.

Entry IV: Headaches

I've been doing a lot of thinking here at camp lately.

Why do some monsters always chase me? Why do most of the maids I meet think only about their next meal and keeping safe? Why did hearing those maids talk about revenge make me feel so terribly uneasy?

And…

Didn't maids used to be like this?

Whenever my thoughts get this far, my head suddenly starts to hurt.
It doesn't feel like ordinary tiredness, or like an injury. It's more like something is stopping me from thinking any further.
A few times I've been right on the verge of remembering something, only for my mind to go completely blank. By the time the pain passes, I've lost my train of thought.

I've tried coming back to it another time. The same thing happens.

Maybe I'm too tired.

But if it's only tiredness, why does it happen only when I think about these things?

Entry V: A Place to Stop for Now

I'm beginning to think I can't go on wandering like this.

I don't know how much farther I can walk, or what I'll come across next. More and more monsters are chasing me, and there are so few maids I can talk to. Even when I do meet one, she may not be willing to trust me.

I need somewhere to stay.

Somewhere safe enough to stop for a while, where I can take my time figuring all this out.

But I can't let on quite so much about myself anymore.
Sometimes I only have to ask a few more questions, or think a little too deeply about something, and the headache comes back.

For now, I've decided to pretend I'm just like the other wandering maids.

Talk less. Think less. If I meet anyone, tell them I'm just looking for food and a place to stay.

If I meet someone kind who's willing to help me, or someone strong enough to keep a place safe, maybe I can stay there for a while.

If there are other maids there too… all the better.

I want to find somewhere I can really settle down.

Somewhere I won't have to run away every day, or worry about when the next attack will come.
If there really is such a place, I hope all the maids I meet from now on can live there.
book.callresponse.outpost_story_recruite: The Five Recruits
The camp leader

Entry I: A Place to Stay for Now

We've been here for a while.

It's no great place, but at least it keeps the wind and rain off, and it's easy to keep an eye on the surroundings. We gathered up what we could use, patched a few things up, and set up a simple watch around the place.

Most days are much the same.

By day we go out looking for targets and fight the creatures that might threaten us. When we get back, it's more training, checking our weapons, and getting ready to go out again.

We haven't forgotten the companions we lost, or why we need to grow stronger.

If we don't want to be hunted down and sent running again, we have to be strong enough to stand our ground.
At the very least, we can't go down so easily again.

Entry II: Uninvited Guests

A group of maids appeared outside camp today.

They didn't look like ordinary wanderers. At their head was a maid I didn't know. There was something unsettling about her. Even from that far off I could feel a great weight bearing down on me.

I couldn't say what it was.

My body knew before I did: she was dangerous.

We weren't about to let them near the camp. I led my sisters in a charge.

And then…

We were no match for her.

She moved astonishingly fast and was far stronger than we were. Even working together, we couldn't really force her back.

By the time I got to my feet again, every one of my sisters was on the ground.

I thought she'd kill us.

She didn't.

She just stood there looking at us. Then she had the maids beside her show us that power.

A purple-black aura surged around them.
It wasn't an ordinary fighting technique, or any ordinary sort of magic. I could feel that power responding to their anger.

Entry III: The Choice She Gave Us

The maid who led them was in no hurry to strike.

She looked at us and asked,

“Do you want to keep running like this?”

I didn't answer.

She had us look again at the maids by her side.

“If you want to grow stronger, follow me.”

“You don't have to be as helpless as you used to be.”

She didn't demand that everyone go with her, or force us to decide then and there. She simply showed us that power.

I admit it. I wavered.

We'd always wanted power. The power to protect ourselves. The power to stop being hunted, to stop losing our companions.

And now that power was right in front of us.

In the end three of my sisters chose to leave with her.

I didn't try to stop them. I knew why they'd made that choice.

Before she left, the maid sent three of her own maids to our camp to take the places of the three who were leaving.

That way we could still hold this place.

Entry IV: The Power She Left Behind

The maid seemed to have planned all this out well in advance.

She had the maids who followed her leave that power here in camp. Those of us who stayed gradually began to feel it, too.

It is powerful. There's no doubt about that.

We're physically stronger now. Even enemies we used to struggle with don't take so much out of us anymore.

We remember what that maid told us before she left:

“Make this place your base. Clear away everything around here that stands in your way.”

“Don't let those things come near your place again.”

With that, she took the other maids and left.
This has been our stronghold ever since.
We began doing what she'd asked. Clearing away nearby threats, attacking anything that might pose a danger to us, and training to get better at using this power.

Entry V: Harder and Harder to Stay Calm

The power really has changed things.

Enemies it used to take several of us to handle are nothing to us now.

But I've also noticed it's getting harder and harder for me to stay calm.

The slightest sound sets me on edge. If someone comes near camp, I strike first. Even after a fight is over, it's hard to shake the anger.

Sometimes there's no reason left to give chase, and I still want to go after them.

I asked the sisters who stayed. They've been feeling much the same.
One said she's always losing her temper lately. Another said she only has to think about what happened to us to want to go settle the score with those things right away.

We all know this power is no ordinary thing.

But none of us is ready to give it up.

Growing stronger is what we've wanted all along, after all.

Entry VI: Our New Sisters

I went to talk to the three sisters who came to the camp later.

Each had her reasons for coming here, too.

One had been chased by monsters and lost her home. Another had been separated from her companions and had fled alone for a long time. Another had seen her own companions killed before her eyes, powerless to do anything.

Every one of them carries hatred in her heart.

They just didn't have the strength before.

They told me they could feel that power, too. Every time they remember what they went through, they feel it all the more clearly.

It suddenly struck me that we might not be the only ones like this.

The sisters who chose to leave with her might be going through the same thing we are.

I just don't know how they're really doing now.

Entry VII: Still Holding Our Post

Someone else passed nearby today.

My sisters picked up their weapons at once.

Looking at them, I suddenly remembered when we first got here.

Back then all we wanted was a place where we could survive.

Now we have strength and a camp we can hold. Even the revenge that once seemed so far away might someday be within reach.

But I don't know where this will all lead if we keep going like this.

All I know is that our work for that maid isn't finished.

This is our stronghold.

We have to clear out every threat around us.

At least while we still have the strength, we can't let anything take this place from us so easily again.

If anyone tries anything, kill them.
book.callresponse.wandering_gly_diary.pa:
My head's spinning. Where am I…? Why is everything square? It's like I've been dropped into Minecraft.

Must be something the Love & Loathing mod does. Wonder what kind of code the author wrote to pull that off…

Somehow I've got a tablet with me. Every time I switch it on, all I get is “No signal.”

There's not a single player here. Just these animals to keep me company…

The tablet finally showed something today: the screen of some Windows 11 PC. The date in the corner says it's the weekend.

The desktop's covered in mod plans, including one for Love & Loathing. Is he the author?
It looks like the tablet only shows anything on weekends. I guess that's the only time the owner gets to use his computer.
He's watching the Love & Loathing camp update video. Lots of people spotted the Easter egg maid. Why does he keep scrolling back and forth?

He replied. I think he wanted people to know he wrote the Easter egg, but nobody seemed to care.

Looks like the PC doesn't belong to JumDa5he, the author of Love & Loathing, after all. This guy's called 51121 or something…

I think I'm rambling. Any player who finds this diary is going to run out of patience halfway through…

I'd still rather find out what's on the tablet. This world is so dull…

He's on GitHub today. His username is gly091020. Turns out 51121 and gly091020 are one and the same. I found him in the Love & Loathing mod credits.

When do I get to stop wandering, anyway? This game is so lonely.

I think that's his QQ. He's answering messages and having a pretty good time in the group chat.

This PC is such a mess. Dozens of projects in IDEA, and the desktop's covered in mods for testing…

I really do sound a bit like him. What's going on?

Today all he did was look through the same photos from middle school, over and over…

I've been here for days now. I've seen plenty of other maids, but they just say the same scripted lines. Pretty boring.

Doesn't look like they can help me…

His NetEase Cloud Music playlist is all Vocaloid. Talk about sticking to one thing.

He's even got a whole folder of favorites just for r-906. He must really like r-906.

I always want to write a little more, but it won't all fit on one Minecraft page. Use two pages and I might run out of paper…

Everything in this world just goes through the motions. I'm getting tired of looking at it…

He opened his MC百科 profile. I didn't know he'd worked on so many mods.

That Maid Doll one looks like it has something to do with maids, too. I wonder if it's installed in this world…

He turned on his mic to record a video today, then forgot to turn it off.

I can hear him sighing at the screen, again and again… I wish I could say something to comfort him…

He really seems to like Iam Music Player Renewed. Brings it up every day…

Forget it. If I keep writing about it, people will think I'm plugging the mod…

First time I've seen what's on his phone. If anything, it's even messier.

There's a bit of everything on there. All kinds of dev tools, all over the place…

Maybe I'll meet someone willing to talk to me. But this world's full of maids who only say what they're programmed to say.

Why isn't there a picture on the tablet today…?

He sure likes putting out hotfixes. Guess his code isn't that great.

He's always coding in the middle of the night. That probably explains the code…

Finally, a player! I rushed up to him…

There was still maid blood on his blade. I got scared and ran for it. At least I didn't lose any of my things.
Looks like this player plans to live nearby. Whenever he sees a Wine Fox, he just cuts her down with one stroke. For some reason he goes easy on the other maids.

The player has the default skin. I wonder if his skin just hasn't loaded, or if that's really how he looks.

I think 51121 uses that very same skin. Surely that's a coincidence…?

He's marked out a building site and filled it with all sorts of machines I don't understand.

And the tablet just happens to have been getting no signal these last few days. Weird…

He rowed his boat slowly off into the distance…

Is he just leaving all those machines? Or maybe he's only gone exploring out at sea…

He never came back… Suddenly I feel so lonely…

The tablet's got a signal again, though. Looks like the last day of the National Day holiday. He's saying goodbye to the group chat…

He's a strange one, too. Happy one minute, sad the next.

The big fat blue fish keeps tapping away at the code. I wonder what he's doing…

I think he's lost patience with making mods. He's writing a note to say updates are slowing down…

I wonder if he'll keep working on Love & Loathing. I want to get out of here…

I don't think I can take much more. The same scenery repeats itself all around me.

I sort of miss that player. Come to think of it, have I ever seen 51121 play a game?

Just my luck. I slipped and rolled down a slope yesterday. Only a few scrapes, thankfully.

I feel like I must be getting close to the world border…
He turned his camera on to film a video. I saw his face! He looks kind of §kscrambled scrambled§r, just like your average high school kid…

I think I've lost the tablet. I'm such an idiot…

Now I'll have to face this lonely world on my own…

I passed a camp today. It was full of maids, so I went up to say hello. They charged straight at me with blades… Scared me to death! Good thing I got away. The one with the snowballs was interesting, though. Doesn't she know snowballs can't hurt anyone?
I wrote down the camp coordinates. Maybe I can steal something later…

One night when the moon was full, I crept into that camp and stole some food. They had more stuff than I could carry…

I sneaked a look at the maid with the snowballs. They'd hung a sign on her chest. Looks like she really isn't popular there either…

I miss that mysterious tablet a bit. I wonder how 51121 is doing.

There's actually a stereo at that camp! You don't see one of those every day. I'll steal it sometime and take a look.
The maid with the sign seems really fond of it. I've seen her fiddling with that stereo every day lately…
Is that… a player? At last! I rushed up…

He had a whole lot of maids on leads! They looked like they were suffering. I got out of there fast. Good thing I can run. Those maids actually talked the way I do, unlike the ones back at camp with their scripted lines. Maybe those are the ones like me…
I think that player's called Koiha_Hotchkiss. I'd better steer clear of him…

Today I woke up the maid with the sign by accident while I was stealing things. I was too scared to move. But she seemed to have noticed something, and she didn't tell me off.

She really is a little like me. No wonder they shut her out…

When we said goodbye, she gave me her stereo…

She mentioned she was out of ink for her diary. I'm almost out myself, though…

This stereo has the exact same playlist as 51121?! That maid's definitely got something to do with him…

Today I passed what looked like a stronghold leading to the End. The End would only be lonelier, though, so I didn't go in.
I think I saw that maid getting told off. Heaven knows why those monsters who do nothing but hit people hate her so much.

I actually saw a squid fall off a waterfall and die when it hit the ground. It dropped some ink sacs, though. My diary's saved!

That night I hurried over to give the ink sacs to that maid. She should be able to write in her diary again…

Those monsters finally found out I'd been stealing from them. They've stepped up their night patrols. Now I'll have to leave.

I hope that strange maid will be all right…

Endless loneliness again… It feels like there's nothing new left…

At least I've still got the stereo that maid gave me. I can play some music to pass the time…
What the heck is “Lava Player failed to load”?! I can't play music anymore… So much for that maid's stereo…

I feel like the loneliness is slowly swallowing me up… I don't want to write anything…

I really wish I could meet a kind player again…
book.callresponse.outpost_story_gly.titl: Is This Really a Home for Five…?
book.callresponse.outpost_story_gly.page: The five of us finally escaped. They put up a camp here. It's a nice enough place, but they always leave me out. I'm no good at anything except throwing snowballs…
Whenever they're talking, I want to go over and say a few words. But they think I say weird things, so they ignore me… At least I still get to eat…
I just sit at home doing nothing. They've each got a job of their own. When they attack intruders, I try throwing snowballs at the enemy, but they all laugh at me…
When I escaped, I stole a stereo from my master. It actually plays music from the real world. None of them seem interested in it, though…
They even brought out three cakes to celebrate today. But when I reached for some, they all gave me a funny look. All I could do was walk away by myself.
It suddenly struck me how they do the same things every day, as if it had all been programmed that way. It's so strange. Then again, I really do seem a little different…
Oh, well. Nobody's likely to find this notebook, so I'll just write it down: somehow I was sent inside a game. That's why I still have some memories of real life…
I remember this camp from Love & Loathing. I guess this is the author's Easter egg… But why would he do this? I'm so miserable here…
I woke up today with a sign hanging on my chest. One of them must be playing a prank. It's fastened to me with iron chains. I can't take it off…
I really want to escape from this home and find a player who'll take me in… They won't even let me use the ink. I probably only have enough left for today's entry…
Ink at last! It's a long story. A mysterious maid gave me some ink sacs, but they found out about her later. I haven't seen her since… I hope she's all right…
I miss my life in the real world a bit. At least my family really loved me. All these monsters ever do is scowl at me…
They keep slaughtering the creatures around here. A few days ago, I saw them kill the maid of a player who was just passing by. Poor thing…
I was afraid they'd notice me, so I threw a few snowballs along with them. That other maid told me snowballs don't hurt people.

They caught me writing in my diary. They snatched it out of my hands, leafed through it and laughed. I felt so humiliated. At least they missed the secret pages. They just tossed the diary on the ground…

I wanted to go find that maid, too, but some mysterious force pulled me back. I might have to stay here forever…

I really wish I could meet a player…

book.callresponse.outpost_story.title: A Home for Five
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.1: Our third night since escaping. Back there, they drove maids to work until they could barely stand. Some never returned from the workshop. Elder Sister says we must survive first. All five of us.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.2: The youngest still has a fever. We gave her the last of our food and took turns helping her walk. Someone mentioned the sisters we left behind. None of us knew what to say.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.3: Once we have a place to stand, we'll save food and weapons and go back for the others. Elder Sister wrote that promise on a scrap of paper. We all pressed our hands to it.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.4: We met a stranger dressed as a maid. We thought she was fleeing too and offered her bread and water. She nearly killed Third Sister. For now, we can trust only each other.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.5: Our first wall is up. Three of us guard the gate and fight; the other two tend the fields and stove. At night, one of our gardeners pores over old papers and parts, seeking a way to see through disguises.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.6: The wheat has grown, and the storeroom isn't empty anymore. At night we mend the wall and dress wounds. By day we each have our work. This place is beginning to feel like home.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.7: A clue at last! She says a few more materials might let us expose any disguise. We all laughed. If it works, perhaps the road to rescue our sisters will be safer.
book.callresponse.outpost_story.page.8: Today everyone is happier than I've seen in ages. Elder Sister says once we have the materials, we can take the next step. We've saved those three cakes for so long. Let's have them tonight, all five of us together.

book.callresponse.wandering_camp_diary.a: A maid who passed this way
book.callresponse.wandering_camp_diary.p:
Ever since I woke up, I've been on the road.

The world is so big. They say there are other maids like me out there. I wonder how they're doing.
Sometimes I find sweet berries. Sometimes I split my last piece of bread and save a little for tomorrow.
Today I found a place to rest. I built a little shelter and laid out a carpet. When the campfire came to life, it felt a little like home.

Some people offer food; others watch from afar.

I haven't seen much of the world. How can I tell who wants to help? Surely not everyone who stops to listen is unkind.

If someone asks me to come along, I'd like to think it over carefully.

If not, I'll gather enough food and set out again.

Perhaps beyond the next mountain, I'll meet a maid willing to travel with me.

For tonight, I'll sleep well. I hope there's enough to eat tomorrow.

memory.callresponse.remnant.01.title: Memory I: The Days We Came Alive
memory.callresponse.remnant.01.content:
Those were fairly happy days.

A few of us maids lived together. We would squabble over food, gather to rest after work, and laugh and tease one another over the smallest things.

Someone would hide the food she had just found, and someone else would discover it and chase after her in a huff. Another would complain that the day's work had been too tiring, sit down to one side, and refuse to get up no matter how much we urged her.

I was one of them.

But there was one maid in our group who always looked troubled. She rarely joined in our games. Often, she would sit alone, staring into the distance.

I went over to her and asked:

“What's wrong? You've looked so worried lately.”

She was silent for a long time before answering softly:

“Don't you think... we've been a little different lately?”

“Different how?”

“A little food makes us happy. Seeing a companion hurt makes us sad. We want to slack off. We get jealous. And we want things that were never ours.”

She raised her head and looked into the distance.

“We've become so alive... Is that a blessing, or a disaster?”

I couldn't understand what she meant.

All I thought was: when you're happy, you laugh; when you're sad, you cry; when you want food, you go and find it. What was wrong with that?

“Why think so much about it? Aren't we all doing pretty well right now?”

She didn't answer. She only looked at me, as if she wanted to say something, then swallowed the words.
memory.callresponse.remnant.02.title: Memory II: Run
memory.callresponse.remnant.02.content:
“Go! Don't look back!”

The monsters' roars came from behind us.

The maid who had always looked so troubled stood at the rear of our group, holding off the pursuing monsters alone. She was wounded, but she wouldn't retreat.

“Run! As long as you survive, that's all that matters!”

We ran for our lives.

I looked back once. She was still standing there. Then the monsters and the rising dust swallowed her from view.

I wanted to stop, but the companion beside me grabbed me.

“We can't go back! She told us to go!”

We could only keep running.

After that day, there was one less of us.
memory.callresponse.remnant.03.title: Memory III: Fewer and Fewer
memory.callresponse.remnant.03.content:
There was no end to our flight.

We moved from place to place, hiding from monsters and from pursuers whose origins we didn't know.

Sometimes we had only just found shelter from the wind and rain when we had to leave again. Some of us were wounded while fleeing. Some never came back from the attacks at night.

Fewer and fewer of the maids who had started out with us remained.

I began to hate those monsters. Whenever I heard their familiar roars, I thought of the ones who had never returned.

I wanted to become stronger.

Strong enough to drive away the things chasing us. Strong enough that I would never have to watch another companion fall.

Strangely, as the anger in my heart grew deeper, I really did seem to grow stronger.

Sometimes I heard voices whose source I couldn't place. It was as if someone were whispering far away, or something were pressed against my ear, answering the thoughts in my heart over and over.

I couldn't make out what the voices said.

But whenever they came, I felt a strange restlessness.

I didn't tell my companions. I only thought that perhaps, at last, I had the strength to protect those who were left.
memory.callresponse.remnant.04.title: Memory IV: A New Companion
memory.callresponse.remnant.04.content:
That day, we met a maid.

She looked no different from us: her clothes were worn, she was covered in dust, and she seemed to have spent a long time on the run too.

She said she had nowhere to go and no companions to rely on.

We talked it over for a while and finally took her in.

One more person meant a little more strength.

At least, that was what we thought then.

After that, the monsters seemed to appear more and more often.

We would find somewhere to stay, only to be attacked soon after. We would evade one group of pursuers, then run into new monsters coming from another direction.

Every time, we could only gather our things in a hurry and run again.

We had no time to think it through.

If monsters came, we ran. If danger approached, we hid. All we could think about was staying alive.

And the maid who had joined us always managed to keep up through the chaos.

I never suspected her.
memory.callresponse.remnant.05.title: Memory V: The Last Campfire
memory.callresponse.remnant.05.content:
After another long stretch of wandering, we finally found somewhere that was safe for the moment.

We were exhausted, with barely enough strength left to speak. Someone lit a fire. Someone brought out what little food remained. We sat around it together and, for once, fell quiet.

I even began to think that perhaps this time we really could rest a little longer.

Then the maid who had joined us later suddenly moved.

She gave no warning. She didn't hesitate.

She lunged at our leader, and her blade plunged into her body.

It all happened too quickly.

The one who had been sitting by the fire just a moment before collapsed. Someone screamed. Someone drew a weapon. Some hadn't even understood what was happening.

The thing pretending to be a maid finally showed its true face.

I didn't know what she really was. I only saw our leader lying in a pool of blood, my companions' terrified faces, and an unfamiliar murderous intent beneath that familiar appearance.

Something burst inside me.

The anger, fear, and grief I had held down for so long surged out together. The power that had been whispering in my ear answered too, and a purple-black aura erupted from my body.

I charged at her.

I don't remember how many times I struck, or what I shouted.

I only knew that I couldn't let her hurt anyone else.

At last, the impostor fell.

But when I came to my senses, no one around me could get back up.

I was the only one left alive.
memory.callresponse.remnant.06.title: Memory VI: Acceptance
memory.callresponse.remnant.06.content:
The campfire had gone out.

I sat there without moving for a long time.

I looked at those familiar figures and tried calling their names. There was no answer.

I thought of the maid who had once stood at the back of our group. I thought of the companions we had lost along the way, and of the impostor who had joined us last, only to destroy everything with her own hands.

At last, I understood that I had nothing left.

That strange power still surrounded me. It offered no comfort and made no promises. It simply kept answering the anger in my heart.

I had once been afraid of it.

But now, I no longer had the strength to be afraid.

“If... having power means this will never happen again...”

I lowered my head, my voice growing softer.

“If I could be so strong that no one could hurt us...”

I paused for a long time.

“Then... take it.”

This time, I didn't refuse.
memory.callresponse.remnant.07.title: Memory VII: Hands That Wouldn't Stop
memory.callresponse.remnant.07.content:
I began searching for answers.

Why could those monsters always find us? Why could we never truly settle down, no matter where we fled? Why had that impostor been able to slip into our group?

I tried to stay calm. I tried to tell who my enemies were. I tried to stop hurting creatures that had nothing to do with any of it.

But whenever monsters came near, the power inside me began to stir.

I would remember my fallen companions, those roars, and the silence beside the campfire where no one answered anymore.

Then the urge to kill overwhelmed my thoughts.

It grew harder and harder to control myself.

Sometimes, only after a fight ended did I realize there was nothing alive around me. Sometimes I couldn't even remember why I had chased something so far.

Once, I passed through a village.

At first, it was only that something had attacked me.

By the time I finally came to my senses, the village was in ruins.

I stood among the broken houses, staring at my hands.

“What... have I done?”

No one answered.

I wanted to stop.

But the power was still surging through me.
memory.callresponse.remnant.08.title: Memory VIII: Those Who Walk Beside Me
memory.callresponse.remnant.08.content:
Later, I met other maids.

Some saw me from a distance, turned in terror, and fled. Some stopped to exchange a few words, then hurried away, unwilling to travel with me.

I didn't understand.

I had become so strong. Strong enough to repel the things that had once chased us.

Why were they still afraid?

Once, I came upon a maid camp.

The maids inside raised their weapons warily. They had clearly already decided I was an enemy.

My instinct was to charge.

But looking at their tense faces, I suddenly remembered the person I had been so long ago.

We had hidden like that too. Fear had made us afraid to trust any stranger.

I stopped.

I didn't kill them. Instead, I used my strength to defeat them one by one, until they could no longer resist.

Only when they finally fell quiet did I speak:

“Has all this running done you any good?”

“Are you hiding here, waiting to be found again?”

I looked at the faces that were still full of hostility.

“I know what you hate.”

“I know that feeling too.”

The purple-black aura around me slowly stirred.

“This power... can keep you from being as helpless as you were before.”

“But it's dangerous. If you accept it, you must be ready for the fact that stopping won't be easy anymore.”

I didn't force anyone.

I simply turned and walked out of the camp.

“If you want to follow, then come.”

“At least... don't wait alone to be killed anymore.”

Hesitant footsteps sounded behind me.

I didn't look back.
memory.callresponse.remnant.09.title: Final Memory: A Place to Return To
memory.callresponse.remnant.09.content:
The last images are already fragmented.

I seem to have fallen somewhere.

The power in me is fading, and the voices in my ears are drifting away.

I see the campfire.

I see my companions sitting around it together.

I see someone secretly hiding the last piece of bread. Someone complaining about how tiring the day has been. Someone else laughing and saying that one day, we'll build a big house.

I try hard to reach out.

“I...”

“Didn't we promise...”

“We'd go home together...?”
